frozen_question: Which components of the nine-gate LONGEVITY SURVIVOR architecture already exist in humans, and which evolved safety/control gates constrain a transition from ordinary REPAIR toward SAFE RENEWAL?
claim_ceiling: Human presence of a pathway does not imply a safe intervention exists.
Animal rejuvenation or regeneration does not establish human efficacy.
Current clinical entry into partial reprogramming establishes testability, not rejuvenation efficacy or whole-body safety.
No dosing, gene-editing, vector-construction or self-experimentation protocol is authorized by this artifact.

core_result.interpretation: The major molecular and cellular classes needed for repair, selective removal, replacement, cancer suppression and state maintenance already exist in humans, but they are tissue-specific, age-dependent, spatially constrained and coupled to tumour-suppression, wound-closure and lineage-fidelity brakes.
core_result.important_correction: The limiting problem is not simply that humans lack regeneration genes. The stronger model is that regenerative capacity is partitioned across tissues and constrained by evolved control systems that prevent uncontrolled proliferation, dedifferentiation and malformed growth.
core_result.why_emergent: A safe renewal program must know where, when, for how long, in which lineage, and after which damage state proliferation/reprogramming may occur, and must terminate after geometry and function are restored. Humans possess many local components but no demonstrated whole-body controller that safely coordinates all nine gates.

human_reverse_gate_matrix.name: DAMAGE_RATE_CONTROL
human_reverse_gate_matrix.limitation: Protection is incomplete and often trades against signalling, immunity and metabolism; damage continues to accumulate with age.

human_reverse_gate_matrix.name: GENOME_REPAIR_AND_CHROMATIN_STABILITY
human_reverse_gate_matrix.limitation: Repair fidelity and capacity vary by cell state and decline or become overwhelmed; mutation-bearing clones can persist even in apparently normal tissues.

human_reverse_gate_matrix.name: CONTROLLED_REPLICATIVE_CAPACITY
examples: telomerase in germline and selected stem/progenitor compartments
human_reverse_gate_matrix.primary_safety_brake: Most somatic cells repress telomerase and use telomere attrition/senescence as part of an anti-neoplastic barrier.

human_reverse_gate_matrix.name: PROTEOSTASIS_AUTOPHAGY_AND_ORGANELLE_QC
human_reverse_gate_matrix.limitation: These systems are finite, context dependent and age-sensitive; chronic nutrient/inflammatory signalling can shift the balance away from maintenance.

human_reverse_gate_matrix.name: IRREPARABLE_CELL_REMOVAL
human_reverse_gate_matrix.primary_safety_brake: Senescence arrests damaged or abnormal cells and is anti-tumour in the short term, but persistent senescent cells and age-weakened immune clearance can become pro-inflammatory and tissue-damaging.

human_reverse_gate_matrix.name: CANCER_SUPPRESSION
human_reverse_gate_matrix.role_in_safe_renewal: This is not an obstacle to remove; it is the central permission system that any regenerative program must preserve.

human_reverse_gate_matrix.name: EPIGENETIC_IDENTITY_PRESERVATION_OR_SAFE_RESET
human_reverse_gate_matrix.primary_safety_brake: Strong lineage identity prevents spontaneous dedifferentiation. Full or poorly controlled reprogramming can erase identity and increase tumour/teratoma risk; partial reprogramming therefore requires strict temporal and lineage control.

human_reverse_gate_matrix.name: TISSUE_AND_SYSTEMIC_HOMEOSTASIS
human_reverse_gate_matrix.primary_safety_brake: Adult mammalian injury often prioritizes rapid sealing and mechanical stability through fibrosis rather than perfect reconstruction. TGF-beta and Hippo/YAP/TAZ sit at the repair-regeneration-cancer boundary.

tissue_evidence_that_human_machinery_exi.developmental_clue: Mammalian cardiac regenerative potential is present neonatally and then sharply reduced; this supports a switched/restricted-program model rather than total genomic absence.

safety_gate_stack_reverse_human.why_it_blocks_unbounded_renewal: Any program that makes old or damaged cells divide more must prove that oncogenic and mutation-bearing clones cannot exploit the same permission.
Regeneration requires plasticity, but excessive plasticity creates loss of cell identity, metaplasia and tumour-like states.
A safe program must stop after the correct number and type of cells have been restored; persistent growth signalling is itself oncogenic/fibrotic.
Limits clonal lifespan and tumour escape, but also limits late-life tissue renewal.
Protects long-lived stem-cell pools from exhaustion and mutation while preventing constant proliferation.
Rapid scar formation can preserve short-term mechanical integrity at the cost of exact tissue reconstruction.
Immune activity is required for debris clearance and cancer control, but chronic inflammation and immune ageing can damage regenerative niches and reduce senescent-cell clearance.

reverse_chain: requires preserved organ geometry and function
requires damage burden below repair+clearance+replacement throughput
D1_CAUSAL_TEMPORAL.delta: The missing unit is not a molecule; it is reliable control of transitions between protected quiescence, temporary regenerative permission, and deterministic shutdown.

mirrors: human liver vs adult human heart: same organism, radically different regenerative permission
neonatal mammalian heart vs adult mammalian heart: similar genome, different developmental state
Turritopsis reset vs human partial reprogramming: functional analogy only, not molecular equivalence
lobster telomerase vs human somatic telomerase repression: opposite implementations around the same renewal/cancer trade-off
D2_HOMOLOG_MIRROR.delta: Cross-tissue differences inside Homo sapiens are stronger evidence for gating than cross-species analogy alone.

D3_ABSTRACTION_HIERARCHY.ascend: SAFE RENEWAL is a permissions-and-termination problem superimposed on repair biology.

D4_ASSOCIATIVE_SEMANTIC.candidate: The human organism may be better described as a mosaic of local regenerative modes rather than one globally repair-only system.

D5_PROVENANCE_AUTHORITY.highest_supported_claim: Humans already possess most component classes needed for regeneration, and multiple of the same systems that protect against cancer or preserve identity also constrain regenerative proliferation/plasticity.
not_supported: a known combination of these gates is safe in humans
partial reprogramming has proven clinical rejuvenation efficacy

claims_attacked.reason: Multiple human tissues regenerate extensively; mammals also retain developmentally restricted regenerative programs.

claims_attacked.claim: Telomerase is the main missing switch.
claims_attacked.reason: Telomerase intersects cancer risk and does not solve identity, genome quality, tissue geometry, fibrosis or termination.

claims_attacked.claim: Cellular senescence is simply bad and should be removed.
claims_attacked.reason: Senescence is a tumour-suppressive and wound/development response as well as a late-life source of dysfunction when cells persist.

claims_attacked.claim: Partial reprogramming proves safe human rejuvenation.
claims_attacked.reason: Preclinical evidence is promising and a first human phase-1 entry exists, but human rejuvenation efficacy and systemic safety are not established.

claims_attacked.claim: Cancer suppression is the only gate.
claims_attacked.reason: Lineage identity, positional information, tissue mechanics, immune state, fibrosis and termination are independently necessary.

demihead_disagreements_preserved: Whether tumour suppression evolved specifically to cause late-life regenerative decline is not established as a single causal explanation; antagonistic pleiotropy is a strong framework, not a universal proof.
Partial reprogramming may rejuvenate selected cellular features while the relation between epigenetic age reversal and durable organismal function remains incomplete.
Telomerase may have functions beyond telomere elongation, but human cancer associations make a universal activation model unacceptable.
Fibrosis can be protective and necessary in acute injury even when it compromises perfect regeneration.
p0_next_gates: Build a within-human tissue matrix comparing HIGH_RENEWAL vs LOW_RENEWAL organs across the same safety-gate variables.
Build a developmental matrix: fetal/neonatal vs adult vs aged tissue to identify which permissions are switched rather than absent.
Separate CELL_REJUVENATION from TISSUE_REGENERATION from ORGANISMAL_LONGEVITY; require independent endpoints for each.
For each candidate mechanism, score benefit and escape modes simultaneously: cancer, fibrosis, loss of identity, stem-cell exhaustion, immune dysregulation and malformed tissue geometry.
Track 2026 human partial-reprogramming phase-1 outcomes as an external test of safety/target engagement; do not infer efficacy before results.
